text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: Elevated HTTP/2 RST_STREAM errors for tenant Silverline on dedicated-pool dl-07. 502/HTTP2 RST code 2 seen from platform->gateway path; client reports intermittent stream resets and truncated streaming responses. Error-rate ~12% over 7m. Paging @oncall.
Maya (oncall): Got the page. Triage starts. Observed symptom: HTTP/2 streams reset mid-response with REFUSED_STREAM (2) and sometimes INTERNAL_ERROR. Is this localized to dl-07?
Ravi (SRE): Yes, only dl-07. Metrics: h2_stream_resets spike at 03:10 UTC, downstream p50 ok, p95 for streaming goes up from 1.2s to 9s, clients report truncated JSON chunks. No recent platform deploys to dl-07.
Sofia (Eng-Platform): Rolling deploys were earlier but none targeted dl-07. Could be a layer 7 proxy interaction with customer's gateway. Any signs of conn resets at TLS level?
Diego (Dedicated Ops): At the TCP layer dl-07 shows many FIN/RST packets originating from the customer gateway IPs. Their gateway IP range: 203.0.113.0/28. We see an increase in HTTP/2 SETTINGS acks and immediate GOAWAYs.
Tess (CS): Silverline support says they started a canary change to Envoy edge config at 03:05 UTC to drop max-concurrent-streams to 50 and enable early stream reset for long-lived streams. They rolled back after 03:20 UTC but damage already done.
silverline-bot: "Alert: Envoy config applied: reduce max-concurrent-streams=50; stream_idle_timeout=15s; retry on reset enabled."
Maya (oncall): That explains it. When their edge reduces max-concurrent-streams, our upstream's in-flight HTTP/2 streams get REFUSED/GOAWAY -> client retries -> dup streams -> resource pressure -> more resets. Need to mitigate quickly. Immediate options: 1) enable per-tenant HTTP/1.1 downgrade for streaming endpoints (force HTTP/1.1 chunked responses), 2) increase platform-side connection pooling to use more parallel connections (bypass their per-conn stream limit), 3) temporarily adjust dl-07 h2_max_concurrent_streams to match their low setting to reduce stream reassigns. Thoughts?
Sofia (Eng-Platform): For safety, do #2 and #1. Increasing parallel connections can be toggled without customer changes. Downgrading to HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming avoids HTTP/2 stream-count semantics and will prevent REFUSED_STREAM behavior. I can flip tenant flag for http2_downgrade_to_h1.
Ravi (SRE): Agree. Also want to enable a short-term client-side dedupe/circuit-breaker: return 429 for duplicate stream attempts within 5s for same session token. That avoids retries creating more load.
Diego (Dedicated Ops): I can spin up additional backend connections on dl-07 and increase upstream connection pool to 10 per worker: ```opsctl pool update dl-07 --upstream-conns 10```
Maya (oncall): I'll execute fallback commands now.
Maya (oncall): ```# enable http1 fallback and per-tenant dedupe
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant silverline --set http2_downgrade_to_h1=true --set stream_dedupe_window=5s
# set circuit breaker to respond 429 for rapid re-streams
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant silverline --set circuit_breaker=true --set cb_response=429
```
Maya (oncall): Commands applied. Noticed immediate drop in RST_STREAMs by ~60% in 90s. Downstream client reports fewer truncated streams.
Tess (CS): Informing Silverline: "We've temporarily downgraded streaming to HTTP/1.1 and enabled short dedupe/circuit-breaker. This avoids interaction with your Envoy stream limits while you revert the canary. Please revert max-concurrent-streams to previous (>=250) and set stream_idle_timeout >= 60s. We can also coordinate a gradual rollout with canary traffic if you want to test lower limits safely."
silverline-bot: "Silverline infra team acknowledges. Rolling back canary now. Will confirm when done."
Sofia (Eng-Platform): Diego, scaling up upstream connections done?
Diego (Dedicated Ops): Pushed: ```opsctl pool update dl-07 --upstream-conns 10``` Workers picked up new socket pools; connection churn small. Watching file descriptors.
Ravi (SRE): Dashboards: p95 streaming latency down to ~2.8s, reset rate to 2% from 12%, truncated-chunk errors nearly gone. Client retry rate also falling after 6m.
Maya (oncall): Handoff to Ravi for sustained monitoring and postmortem. I'm stepping off. @Ravi you'll own the follow-ups.
Ravi (SRE): Taking over. Action items: - CS/Tess to collect Silverline's Envoy config and rollout timeline, - Eng-Platform/Sofia to add a safe-guard that triggers http1 fallback when h2_reset_rate > 5% for 5m, - Ops/Diego to keep upstream_conns increased for 30m then scale down gradually.
Tess (CS): Silverline confirmed rollback of canary at 03:27 UTC and reports stable streams after ~8 minutes. They will share Envoy config and canary plan.
Sofia (Eng-Platform): I'll create a docs snippet: recommended envoys settings when fronting long-lived streams: max_concurrent_streams >= 200, stream_idle_timeout >= 60s, and avoid aggressive per-conn stream quotas for backend traffic. Also will add a platform feature request: per-tenant automatic http1-fallback trigger and runbook.
Ravi (SRE): Filing SEV2 postmortem stub and tagging this thread. Short RCA: customer canary reduced HTTP/2 concurrency & short stream idle timeout -> platform HTTP/2 stream resets and client retries -> stream truncation and higher errors. Mitigation: tenant-level HTTP/1.1 fallback, increase upstream connections, circuit-breaker for duplicate stream attempts.
Diego (Dedicated Ops): Will keep dl-07 extra upstreams for 40m. No tenant isolation breach detected; no user data exposure.
incident-bot: Paging suppressed. Incident marked mitigated pending RCA write-up.
Ravi (SRE): Closing active mitigation. Next steps already assigned; will follow up with a full SEV2 doc in /incidents/postmortems and link here. Thanks team. :wave:
